findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of the address gets around the block.
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match in Postgres. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` finds no record, `should_block?` returns false, and the registration goes through. The validator gets the raw attribute value. I can't see whether User downcases the email before validation runs. Fix: store blocked emails in lowercase and compare with `where('lower(email) = ?', email.downcase)`, or downcase both sides.

findings.title: The match_count update reads, adds and writes back, so concurrent matches overwrite each other.
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the count, adds one and writes the whole value back. When two signups with the same blocked email are validated at the same time, both read N and both write N+1, so one match is lost. Also, every `valid?` call on the user increments the counter, so a single signup that validates more than once is counted more than once. Use an atomic update instead: `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.
